newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Rabobank plans to begin securitisation in 1998.
newsitem.headline: Rabobank plans to begin securitisation in 1998.

text.p: Dutch cooperative bank Rabobank Nederland plans to move some of its assets off balance sheet by securitising them from next year, executive board chairman Herman Wijffels said on Wednesday.

He said the bank, which has no outside shareholders from which to raise new capital for credit growth, had syndicated some of its loans last year in a bid to limit the lending growth which puts pressure on its limited capital.
"We are also planning to move into securitisation," he told Reuters after a news conference to announce the bank's 1996 profit results.
The bank's lending grew 14 percent in calendar 1996, higher than in the first half of 1996 and above the normal level of eight to nine percent per year.
At the time of the bank's half-year results last August, Wijffels said Rabobank was reducing its new lending in a bid to maintain its strong capitalisation ratios.
Asked about this process, he said the bank had syndicated to other banks about 5.0-6.0 billion of the 26.5 billion guilders of new lending made to consumers and companies in 1996.
Wijffels said this represented a change in Rabobank's practice of taking all its loans on the balance sheet.

Wijffels said the bank would probably securitise mortgages, consumer credits and trade finance loans, among other types of lending. But he declined to specify what proportion of total assets would be taken off balance sheet.
He said Rabobank was looking to take this action because its capacity to generate new loans was larger than its capacity to carry loans on its balance sheet.

Another reason for securitisation was the expected continued narrowing of interest rate spreads in the future. "You can look upon securitisation as a way of increasing efficiency...by earning enough to keep your BIS ratio at reasonable levels."

Rabobank's BIS ratio stood at 11.3 percent at the end of 1996, down from 12.0 percent a year earlier but above the minimum requirement of eight percent. -- Garry West, Amsterdam Newsroom +31 20 504 5000
